title: Load-replay sampler and decayed-percentile explorer for per-route/model/region quantiles
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a load-replay sampling harness plus a "decayed-percentile" explorer to produce reliable p95/p99 signals per route/model/region. The goal is to run reproducible, cost-efficient regressions against production-like traffic slices (tokens/sec, context length distribution, and KV-cache-hit characteristics) and to expose time-series dashboards and alerts that surface statistically significant regressions at p95/p99. This work covers: the sampler that selects representative requests, the playback harness that reproduces token throughput and KV cache state, the quantile computation pipeline with time-decay weighting, and dashboard widgets + alert rules per (route, model, region).
acceptance_criteria: Sampler can take a 24h traffic window and produce a 1h test trace with matched tokens/sec and context-length CDFs for a given route/model/region
Playback harness supports KV-cache warmup and replays token timing with +/-15% fidelity on tokens/sec for target slices
Quantile pipeline computes rolling p95/p99 with exponential decay (half-life configurable) and stores daily and hourly rollups for route/model/region
Dashboards show p50/p95/p99, sample count, tokens/sec, and KV-warmup ratio by route/model/region with drilldowns to raw traces
Regression detector raises an alert when p95 or p99 degrades above configurable thresholds (absolute ms and relative %) and auto-opens a regression ticket with attached baseline and replay diff
tasks: Design sampler algorithm (stratified reservoir sampling by route/model/region + tokens/sec bins)
Implement trace exporter from production ingestion stream (redwood-telemetry -> replay store)
Build playback harness that can run on dedicated infra and emulate batching/kv-warmup
Add decayed-percentile aggregation jobs to telemetry pipeline (hourly), store in clickhouse/rollups table
Create Grafana dashboards per route/model/region and templated alerting rules
Add CI job to run nightly baseline playback and regression detection against canary model variants
decisions: Use stratified reservoir sampling instead of naive tail-sampling to preserve rare long-context requests and avoid p99 bias
Implement exponential time decay for quantile rollups (default half-life = 7 days) so recent regressions have higher weight without losing long term context
Playback will run in a sandboxed Dedicated pool to ensure deterministic GPU scheduling; we will not attempt full production traffic shaping in-hosted lanes initially
Store rollups in ClickHouse to leverage existing rollup/aggregation patterns and fast per-route queries; use a compact schema keyed by (date_hour, route, model, region)
tradeoffs: Reservoir sampling preserves distribution but requires more memory in the sampler; acceptable cost for fidelity
Running playback in Dedicated increases infra spend; tradeoff accepted to achieve deterministic latency comparisons vs noisy multi-tenant clusters
Time-decay makes older regressions less visible over time — mitigated by keeping a separate long-term baseline snapshot for forensic comparisons
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: initial design doc posted to Confluence and shared with platform team: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Load+Replay+Sampler
2026-03-04: prototype sampler implemented (reservoir + tokens/sec bucketing) and validated on a 12h window; sample fidelity: KS-distance < 0.06 for context-length and tokens/sec distributions
2026-03-07: playback harness PoC able to warm KV and replay 5k tokens/sec trace on a single V100-equivalent node; observed median latency within 10% of production baseline for same model
2026-03-09: quantile aggregator job skeleton merged (PR #4820) and small hourly rollups written to dev ClickHouse cluster
review_feedback: PM (Jenna Morales): prefer lower default decay half-life (7d) to make regressions more visible for fast-moving models
SRE (Liam O'Neill): recommend adding a runbook for playback failures and automatic teardown of sandbox nodes to avoid cost leaks
Design (Rina Gupta): add a dashboard panel that overlays replay vs production p95/p99 for visual regression confirmation
notes: Next: wire alerting into Slack + optionally open a regression ticket via automation when threshold breached
Consider adding synthetic adversarial traces (long context + high-burst tokens/sec) for stress-tests after GA
Follow-up: integrate with Eval harness to tie latency regressions to model-quality regressions (semantic drift)
